re_line: Solomons Opposition alleges Australian interference · Canberra publishes Naoero NZYQ deal · algorithm opt-out bill lands · China pushes Pacific policing · NZDF seeks closer Australian ties
morning_memo: Solomon Islands' Opposition accused Australia of foreign interference over a leaked text message to Deputy Prime Minister Francis Sade, days after a no-confidence motion lapsed and Canberra agreed in principle to a billion-dollar treaty package.

Canberra published the terms of its NZYQ deportation agreement with Naoero covering more than 350 people, with Green Party senator David Shoebridge saying the government still withholds the separate memorandum setting up the financial arrangement.

China called for more practical results with Pacific Island countries on police capacity building, Xinhua reported, as Fiji's immigration ministry insisted Australia will get no backdoor access to its new border system.

top_stories.headline: Solomon Islands Opposition alleges Australian interference as treaty deal lands
top_stories.body: Solomon Islands' Opposition says a leaked message between the Australian High Commission and Deputy Prime Minister Francis Sade appeared to show Australian funding being used to influence the outcome of a no-confidence motion against the prime minister. Sade rejected the claim, saying the text was an update on successful treaty negotiations and should not be used as political ammunition. The motion was withdrawn just as negotiations wrapped up, with Australia agreeing in principle to a billion-dollar package. Lowy Institute research fellow Oliver Nobetau said the common thread across recent bilateral agreements is language on denying strategic access to third parties.
top_stories.src_line: per ABC Pacific: "Solomon Islands Opposition accuses Australia of foreign interference" · also Sydney Morning Herald (Matthew Knott)

top_stories.headline: Albanese unveils algorithm opt-out under Digital Duty of Care bill
top_stories.body: Anthony Albanese confirmed Australians will be able to choose between existing recommendation algorithms and their "following feed" under new online safety legislation branded "my feed, my way". The Coalition and right-wing politicians have called the package politically motivated censorship, and AFP reported the government is threatening hefty fines where platforms fail the duty of care. The AFR noted the announcement lands as US technology companies face higher Australian tax bills.
top_stories.src_line: per Reuters: "Australia targets social media algorithms with new user-choice rules" · also Australian Financial Review

top_stories.headline: Canberra releases NZYQ deportation agreement with Naoero
top_stories.body: The Australian government released the agreement to deport more than 350 refugees and asylum seekers, the "NZYQ cohort", to Naoero, formerly Nauru. Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke said in August 2025 that the deal gave Naoero AU$2.5 billion over thirty years. Green Party senator David Shoebridge said the release only scratches the surface, that the government "has been far from forthright", and that it continues to resist producing a separate memorandum establishing the financial arrangement.
top_stories.src_line: per RNZ Pacific: "'New level of bastardry': Australia releases NZYQ agreement with Naoero"

overnight_items.headline: Israel warns Canberra against following UK settlement sanctions
overnight_items.body_text: Israel's ambassador warned that broad sanctions on settlements would be a deep mistake, as pressure builds on Canberra to match the United Kingdom, France and Canada, which have announced bans on imports from Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank. The three governments said in a joint statement that rising settler violence poses a "direct and urgent threat" to a two-state solution. Foreign Minister Penny Wong has said Australia is not pursuing a blanket import ban.

overnight_items.headline: Foreign network deepfakes dozens of Australian politicians on Facebook
overnight_items.body_text: Reset Tech tracked more than 200 Facebook pages impersonating Anthony Albanese, Angus Taylor, Pauline Hanson and other figures over the past eight months, linking the network to an influencer business in Sri Lanka. Roughly 10 percent of the pages have been monetised through Facebook's creator payment scheme. "This isn't foreign interference as we traditionally think of it," said Reset Tech chief research officer Rys Farthing.

overnight_items.headline: Economists flag back-to-back rate rises after Hauser warning
overnight_items.body_text: Economists moved to forecasts of consecutive increases after Reserve Bank deputy governor Andrew Hauser used a rare television interview to say inflation and growth were both still too high and that the economy is running stronger than expected. The cash rate has been on hold at 4.35 percent since the unanimous decision of 11 August 2026, a second consecutive hold after three increases earlier this year.

pacific_wire.headline: Fiji says Australia gets no backdoor into new border system
pacific_wire.body_text: Permanent Secretary for Immigration Aliki Salusalu said Fiji will fully own and operate the Migration Enforcement and Response Intelligence Tool, introduced through the Vuvale Partnership with Australia, when it replaces the Integrated Border Management System next year. "It will be a fully closed system," he said, adding there would be no backdoor access for anyone without the ministry's knowledge.

pacific_wire.headline: Vanuatu launches review of presidential pardon powers
pacific_wire.body_text: Minister of Justice Job Andy launched the Vanuatu Law Reform Commission report on pardon administration, a review begun in 2020. VLRC principal legal researcher Gracelyn Tasso said the absence of any legislative framework around the President's Article 38 power has produced perceptions of inconsistency and political influence, and left Vanuatu known as the "pardoning capital of the Pacific".

pacific_wire.headline: Samoa signs US$3 million ADB-funded vaccine and equipment package
pacific_wire.body_text: Prime Minister La'aulialemalietoa Leuatea Polataivao Fosi Schmidt, acting as Minister of Health, signed for US$2,965,497 in medical equipment, supplies and specialised trucks under the Asian Development Bank-funded Systems Strengthening for Effective Coverage of New Vaccines in the Pacific project. The project also covers Tonga, Tuvalu and Vanuatu, and UNOPS will run the procurement.

pacific_wire.headline: Bank of PNG holds Kina Facility Rate at 5.0 percent
pacific_wire.body_text: The Bank of Papua New Guinea's Monetary Policy Committee kept the Kina Facility Rate at 5.0 percent and the Cash Reserve Requirement at 9.0 percent following its September 2026 meeting.

pacific_wire.headline: Timor-Leste hosts WHO regional committee as malaria-free status draws praise
pacific_wire.body_text: Health leaders gathered in Timor-Leste for the South East Asia WHO Regional Committee commended the host for becoming malaria free. The same program reported that more than 300 unexploded World War Two ordnances were destroyed on Betio Island in Kiribati over the weekend.

pacific_wire.headline: New Caledonia wins French bailout as financial crisis deepens
pacific_wire.body_text: Islands Business's PACNEWS bulletin reports New Caledonia has secured a French bailout as its financial crisis worsens. The same bulletin carries Japan and UNDP partnering on inclusive elections in Solomon Islands, and Pacific leaders being urged to keep the Bougainville question internal.

pacific_wire.headline: Fiji civil society warns on surveillance powers in Police Bill 2026
pacific_wire.body_text: The Fiji Council of Social Services told Parliament's Standing Committee on Justice, Law and Human Rights that surveillance, tracking and biometric powers in the proposed Fiji Police Bill 2026 could be turned on civil society groups, political opponents and journalists. Programme manager Josaia Tokoni pointed to clauses 57 and 62, a new biometric database, and an offence of causing "disaffection" among police staff that he said could criminalise genuine criticism.

pacific_wire.headline: PNG debate turns on whether Bougainville sets a precedent
pacific_wire.body_text: The National argues Section 276 of the Constitution ensures no province other than Bougainville can pursue the path in Part XIV, which constitutionalised the 2001 Bougainville Peace Agreement. Mt Hagen MP William Duma told Parliament that Section 2 makes the unity of the state absolute. The 2019 referendum returned 97.7 percent for independence.

pacific_wire.headline: Fiji Airways opens second Sydney gateway from March 19, 2027
pacific_wire.body_text: Fiji Airways will fly Nadi to Western Sydney International Airport three times weekly from March 19, 2027, using 737 MAX 8 aircraft and adding about 53,000 seats a year. Chief executive Paul Scurrah said the region is home to one of the largest Fijian communities outside Fiji. The announcement came as Fiji passed one million visitors in a 12-month period for the first time.

new_zealand.headline: Wellington drops royalties on stored gas to unlock storage projects
new_zealand.body_text: Resources Minister Shane Jones said the government will end the requirement for developers to pay royalties on gas unlikely to be extracted or sold, removing a barrier to underground storage. Jones said proposals already being explored could significantly expand New Zealand's storage capacity, which he framed as bridging winter and dry-year peaks in electricity demand.

new_zealand.headline: Wellington officials say staffing gaps compromised flood response
new_zealand.body_text: Wellington City Council's Civil Defence controller told councillors that a lack of trained emergency operation centre staff compromised the response to the 20 April flash flooding, in which one man died and more than one hundred homes were affected. Emergency management and city development manager Phil Becker said capability at staff level was "very variable" and warned there are not enough skilled people to handle a larger disaster.

china_in_the_pacific.headline: Beijing presses for more practical results in Pacific police cooperation
china_in_the_pacific.body_text: Xinhua reported China called for more practical results with Pacific Island countries in police capacity building and cooperation. The state agency gave no further specifics on countries or programmes in the item carried.

china_in_the_pacific.headline: Vanuatu op-ed answers US deputy secretary of state on the state of the friendship
china_in_the_pacific.body_text: Responding to an editorial by Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau, the piece acknowledges American wartime infrastructure on Efate and Santo, decades of Peace Corps service, and Millennium Challenge Corporation funding for the Efate Ring Road and Santo East Coast Road. It then lists the complications: unexploded wartime ordnance, the unresolved consequences of American nuclear testing in the Marshall Islands, and US commercial mining interests whose profits leave the region.

canberra_politics.headline: Native forest carbon credit scheme splits Greens from environmental groups
canberra_politics.body_text: A proposed native forest carbon credit scheme has divided the Greens and environmental organisations, presenting an early test for leader Larissa Waters, The Australian reported.

canberra_politics.headline: AFP files top secret evidence seen only by the judge in Avalon hijacking case
canberra_politics.body_text: The Australian Federal Police has submitted classified material in the Avalon airport hijacking prosecution that will be seen only by the presiding judge, The Australian reported.

business_economy.headline: RBA sees slowdown, not recession, from the housing downturn
business_economy.body_text: Reserve Bank assistant governor Sarah Hunter said the housing downturn is hitting related sectors but rejected a developer's warning of recession. The Australian reported separately that analysts have updated forecasts to price declines of up to 15 percent.

business_economy.headline: National tax take up 60 percent since Covid to $893 billion
business_economy.body_text: Combined federal, state and territory tax collections have risen 60 percent since the pandemic to $893 billion, The Australian reported.

business_economy.headline: American money and technology move into Australia's shale patch
business_economy.body_text: US operators are bringing capital, technology and lessons from the American shale boom into Australia's shale acreage, Reuters reported.

business_economy.headline: Labor's trust tax changes carry a levy on newborns, paper reports
business_economy.body_text: The Australian reports that Labor's proposed changes to trust taxation create an unflagged charge affecting newborn beneficiaries, a detail not set out when the measure was announced.

primary_documents.headline: NZDF and Ngati Rangi sign agreement for 50 homes at Waiouru
primary_documents.body_text: Defence Minister Paul Goldsmith announced the New Zealand Defence Force and iwi Ngati Rangi have signed an agreement enabling construction of 50 new homes at Waiouru Military Camp, honouring commitments under the Ngati Rangi Treaty settlement. Buildings and land are sold to the iwi and leased back under a long-term arrangement, with completion expected by mid-2028. Further homes are progressing at Devonport, Wellington, Whenuapai, Christchurch and Manawatu.
primary_documents.key_line: This agreement will strengthen the meaningful partnership NZDF has with Ngāti Rangi, and respects the important role the iwi plays in the future of the land.

calendar_watch.event: New Zealand general election, advance voting from 26 October
calendar_watch.why_it_matters: Decides whether the National, ACT and NZ First coalition continues, and with it current defence and Pacific settings.

calendar_watch.event: Signature of the Australia-Solomon Islands treaty agreed in principle
calendar_watch.why_it_matters: Canberra has agreed in principle to a billion-dollar package that Honiara's Opposition says is entangled with a failed no-confidence motion.
Tonga's meteorological service has been pressing regional media to convert warnings into action before the season opens.

calendar_watch.event: First application of the Pacific Islands Forum's new dialogue partner model, in New Zealand
calendar_watch.why_it_matters: Sets the precedent for how the two-tier partner system agreed at Koror handles external powers seeking Forum access.

calendar_watch.event: Fiji Airways begins Nadi to Western Sydney International Airport services
calendar_watch.why_it_matters: Adds a second Sydney gateway and about 53,000 seats a year to the Australia-Fiji route.

also_today.headline: Affirmed, noted, endorsed: Pacific Islands Forum leaders in Koror
also_today.body_text: Tess Newton Cain and Stefan Armbruster write that a ballistic missile test and China-Taiwan tensions took the headlines, but PIFLM55 in Palau delivered a two-tier dialogue partner system, the Belau Declaration, and commitments on artificial intelligence, gender and renewable energy.

also_today.headline: PALM welfare support extensive on paper, poorly connected in practice
also_today.body_text: A Devpolicy policy brief finds the Pacific Australia Labour Mobility welfare system is broad but poorly understood. Approved Employers must provide a Welfare Officer at one full-time equivalent per 120 workers, with the PALM Guidelines 2.1 of 27 March 2026 setting out 56 "must" and four "must not" statements across 11 pages. Because the officer is engaged by the employer, workers may fear that raising a concern jeopardises their job.

also_today.headline: Vanuatu regulator issues revised broadcasting code
also_today.body_text: The Telecommunications, Radiocommunications and Broadcasting Regulator launched an updated Code of Practice for Broadcasting and Media Services covering fairness, privacy and programme content. Regulator Jesse Benjamin said the revision responds to new platforms and the growth of social media.

also_today.headline: Fiji MPs question sugar subsidies as cane tonnage falls
also_today.body_text: Standing Committee on Economic Affairs chairperson Sakiusa Tubuna said support to the sugar industry "is not yielding the return", noting that 20 percent of farmers produce 80 percent of cane tonnage while subsidies go to all. Officials said fertiliser subsidies were cut from $20 million to $15 million last year without knowing the effect on yields.

also_today.headline: PNG graduates take up UK Chevening scholarships
also_today.body_text: Top Papua New Guinean university graduates have been awarded Chevening scholarships and travel to the United Kingdom to begin master's study later this month, the Post-Courier reported.
